france/monthelie.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy, making more than 85% red wine from Pinot Noir and the rest white from Chardonnay. It has no Grand Cru vineyards, and most of its white wines are 100% Chardonnay.

france/montlouis-sur-loire.text: A Loire Valley appellation for wines made from Chenin, from three communes including Montlouis-sur-Loire itself. It allows still wine, semi-sparkling wine and quality sparkling wine.

france/montrachet.text: A Côte de Beaune Grand Cru appellation in Burgundy for white wine made only from Chardonnay. It covers vineyards in the two communes of Chassagne-Montrachet and Puligny-Montrachet.

france/montravel.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France for white wines from Sauvignon, Semillon and Muscadelle, and for Merlot-led reds.

france/morey-saint-denis.text: A Côte de Nuits village in Burgundy, around 96% red from Pinot Noir and a little white from Chardonnay. It holds five Grand Cru vineyards, including Clos de Tart, Clos des Lambrays, Clos Saint-Denis and Clos de la Roche.

france/morgon.text: A Beaujolais appellation in the commune of Villié-Morgon, making red wine from Gamay.

france/moulin-a-vent.text: A Beaujolais cru for red wine from Gamay, on the border of the Rhône and Saône-et-Loire departments, in parts of Chénas and Romanèche-Thorins. Its name means windmill, and it gained AOC status in 1936.

france/moulis-en-medoc.text: A Médoc appellation in Bordeaux for red wine, made from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and other Bordeaux grapes. It covers Moulis-en-Médoc and four neighboring communes.

france/muscadet.text: A white wine from the Pays nantais at the western end of the Loire Valley, made from the Melon de Bourgogne grape, often called simply Melon. The name refers to a supposed musky taste, though the wines show little of it.

france/muscadet-coteaux-de-la-loire.text: A Loire Valley appellation for white wine made only from Melon, grown in fifteen communes along the river around Ancenis-Saint-Géréon, Oudon and Le Cellier.

france/muscadet-cotes-de-grandlieu.text: A Muscadet appellation for white wine made only from Melon, grown in communes around Saint-Philbert-de-Grand-Lieu and Sainte-Pazanne.

france/muscadet-sevre-et-maine.text: A Muscadet appellation for white wine made only from Melon, from thirty communes around Vallet, Clisson and Vertou.

france/muscat-de-beaumes-de-venise.text: A Rhône Valley appellation for wine made from Muscat à Petits Grains, white or gray. It comes from the communes of Beaumes-de-Venise and Aubignan.

france/muscat-de-frontignan.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for liqueur wine made from Muscat à Petits Grains, white or red. It comes from the communes of Frontignan and Vic-la-Gardiole in Hérault.

france/muscat-de-lunel.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation in Hérault for liqueur wine made from Muscat à Petits Grains. It covers four communes, including Lunel and Lunel-Viel.

france/muscat-de-mireval.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation in Hérault for liqueur wine made from Muscat à Petits Grains. It covers the communes of Mireval and Vic-la-Gardiole.

france/muscat-de-rivesaltes.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation, in the Roussillon area, for white fortified sweet wines, a style called vin doux naturel. They are made from Muscat d'Alexandrie and Muscat à Petits Grains, usually in equal parts, with at least 100 grams per liter of sugar. Often served as an aperitif.

france/muscat-de-saint-jean-de-minervois.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for liqueur wine made from white Muscat à Petits Grains. It comes from a single commune, Saint-Jean-de-Minervois, in Hérault.

france/musigny.text: A Grand Cru in the commune of Chambolle-Musigny in the Côte de Nuits, made from Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It is the only Côte de Nuits Grand Cru making both red and white, with red over 90% of output.

france/mutigny.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/northern-rhone.text: A Rhône Valley area holding Côte-Rôtie, Hermitage, Cornas, Saint-Joseph, Crozes-Hermitage and Condrieu.

france/nuits-saint-georges.text: A Côte de Nuits village in Burgundy, about 97% red from Pinot Noir and a little white from Chardonnay. Its name comes from the Latin for walnuts, and it has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/oger.text: A cru village in the Côte des Blancs, a Champagne sub-region whose vineyards are 95% Chardonnay.

france/oiry.text: A cru village in the Côte des Blancs, a Champagne sub-region whose vineyards are 95% Chardonnay.

france/orleans.text: A Loire Valley appellation around the city of Orléans, making wine from Chardonnay, Meunier and Pinot Noir. Pinot Gris is allowed as a minor grape.

france/orleans-clery.text: A Loire Valley appellation near Orléans for red wine made only from Cabernet Franc. It covers five communes, including Cléry-Saint-André and Olivet. Cabernet Franc is the Loire's main red grape, especially around Chinon.

france/pacherenc-du-vic-bilh.text: A South West France appellation for white wine, sweet or dry, made from Petit Manseng, Gros Manseng and Petit Courbu, with Arrufiac, Courbu and Sauvignon allowed as minor grapes. It covers 37 communes, including Arricau-Bordes, Aydie and Crouseilles.

france/palette.text: A small Provence appellation near Aix-en-Provence, set up in 1948. It covers Aix-en-Provence, Meyreuil and Le Tholonet, and allows many grapes, led by Grenache, Mourvèdre and Cinsaut for red and Clairette and Bourboulenc for white.

france/pargny-les-reims.text: A cru village in Champagne, whose sparkling wines are made from Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Meunier and a few rarer grapes.

france/pauillac.text: A Haut-Médoc commune in Bordeaux for red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and other Bordeaux grapes. It has three of the five premier cru châteaux: Latour, Lafite Rothschild and Mouton Rothschild.

france/pays-d-oc-igp.text: A regional IGP covering the whole Languedoc-Roussillon vineyard, formerly called vin de pays d'Oc. It is the largest IGP in France and one of the most popular French wines.

france/pecharmant.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France, for red wine from the hills northeast of Bergerac, made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon and Cot. It covers about 990 acres and is called the best known wine of the Dordogne.

france/pernand-vergelesses.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making a little more than half red from Pinot Noir and the rest white from Chardonnay. Its western Corton hill side has vineyards of all three Corton Grand Crus.

france/pessac-leognan.text: The northern part of Graves in Bordeaux, equally known for red and dry white wines, though red leads. It includes Château Haut-Brion, and its classed growths make about a third of its wine.

france/petit-chablis.text: A Burgundy appellation in the Chablis area for white wine made only from Chardonnay, around Chablis and sixteen other communes in Yonne. Chablis is Burgundy's northernmost appellation, with a cool climate that gives acidity and sometimes a flinty note.

france/picpoul-de-pinet.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon white wine appellation in Hérault, made only from Piquepoul. It comes from six communes around Pinet, including Mèze and Montagnac.

france/pierrevert.text: A Provence appellation covering eleven communes around Manosque and Pierrevert. It allows many grapes, including Grenache, Syrah, Carignan and Mourvèdre for red and Grenache Blanc, Vermentino, Marsanne and Roussanne for white.

france/pierry.text: A Champagne village rated as a cru, in the region that makes Quality Sparkling Wine.

france/pomerol.text: A Right Bank commune in Bordeaux whose wine is mostly Merlot with Cabernet Franc in support. It has no real village, just a church among the vines, and became AOC in 1936.

france/pommard.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making red wine only, mainly from Pinot Noir. It has no Grand Cru vineyards but several highly regarded Premier Crus, and the AOC dates from 1936.

france/pouilly-fuisse.text: The best-known part of the Mâconnais, a white wine appellation made only from Chardonnay in Fuissé, Solutré-Pouilly, Vergisson and Chaintré. It gained premier cru status in 2020, with 22 premier cru climats.

france/pouilly-fume.text: A Loire Valley appellation around Pouilly-sur-Loire in Nièvre for dry white wine made from Sauvignon Blanc.

france/pouilly-loche.text: A Mâconnais appellation for white wine made only from Chardonnay, in Loché, an associated commune of Mâcon. It has one premier cru, Les Mûres, and sits next to Pouilly-Fuissé and Pouilly-Vinzelles.

france/pouilly-sur-loire.text: A Loire Valley appellation for white wine made from Chasselas, around Pouilly-sur-Loire in Nièvre. It shares its communes with Pouilly-Fumé, which is made from a different grape.

france/pouilly-vinzelles.text: A Mâconnais appellation for white wine made only from Chardonnay, in Vinzelles and Loché. It has no premier cru vineyards and sits next to Pouilly-Fuissé and just south of Pouilly-Loché.

france/premieres-cotes-de-bordeaux.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers, across thirty-nine communes including Bassens, Baurech and Bouliac. Its wines are made from Sémillon, Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle.

france/provence.text: A region of southeast France where wine has been made for at least 2,600 years, since the Greeks founded Marseille. It holds Bandol, Cassis, Bellet and Côtes de Provence.

france/puisieulx.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils and nine Grands Crus villages.

france/puisseguin-saint-emilion.text: A Bordeaux Right Bank appellation for red wine, from the commune of Puisseguin. It is made from Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Cot, with Carmenère and Petit Verdot allowed as minor grapes.

france/puligny-montrachet.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy making almost only white wine, about 99.5%, from Chardonnay. It has four Grand Cru vineyards, with Montrachet the best known, and 17 Premier Crus.

france/quarts-de-chaume.text: A Loire Valley appellation for wine made only from Chenin, grown in the single commune of Rochefort-sur-Loire. Most Loire Valley production is white, from Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Melon.

france/quincy.text: A Loire Valley appellation for dry white wine, made from Sauvignon in two communes, Quincy and Brinay, in Cher.

france/rasteau.text: A southern Rhône appellation covering fortified and unfortified wines, led by Grenache. Sweet fortified wines can be red, rosé or white. Dry red wines were added in 2010 and now make up 97% of production.

france/regnie.text: A Beaujolais appellation for red wine made from Gamay, with Aligoté, Chardonnay and Melon also allowed. It covers the communes of Régnié-Durette and Lantignié.

france/reuilly.text: A Loire Valley appellation in Cher and Indre, with wines made from Sauvignon, Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris.

france/rhone-valley.text: A wine region of France with Northern Rhône and Southern Rhône inside it, plus areas such as Cairanne, Vinsobres and Costières de Nîmes.

france/richebourg.text: A Grand Cru in Vosne-Romanée in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine mainly from Pinot Noir. It borders La Romanée and Romanée-Conti to the south, and the AOC was created in 1936.

france/right-bank.text: A Bordeaux area holding Saint-Émilion Grand Cru, Pomerol, Fronsac, Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux and Côtes de Bourg.

france/rilly-la-montagne.text: A Champagne village rated as a cru, in the region that makes Quality Sparkling Wine.

france/rivesaltes.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation in the Roussillon area for naturally sweet fortified wine, a style called vin doux naturel. It is made from Grenache, Grenache Blanc, Grenache Gris, Macabeu and Tourbat, with Muscat also allowed, across 94 communes.

france/romanee-conti.text: A Grand Cru vineyard in Vosne-Romanée in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine from Pinot Noir. It is a monopole of the Domaine de la Romanée-Conti, and its wine is among the most sought after and expensive in the world.

france/romanee-saint-vivant.text: A Grand Cru in Vosne-Romanée in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine mainly from Pinot Noir. It takes its name from the Abbey of Saint Vivant, which owned several vineyards here in medieval times.

france/rose-d-anjou.text: A Loire Valley rosé appellation made from Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Gamay, Grolleau, Cot and Pineau d'Aunis. It covers 88 communes in Anjou.

france/rose-de-loire.text: A Loire Valley rosé appellation made from Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Gamay, Grolleau, Pineau d'Aunis and Pinot Noir. It spans 246 communes.

france/rose-des-riceys.text: A rosé from the three villages of Les Riceys in the Aube, in Champagne, made only from Pinot Noir. It can be tank-fermented for early drinking or wood-fermented for ageing, and has a distinctive taste the French call goût des Riceys.

france/rosette.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France for white wine, made from Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris, Semillon and Muscadelle. It covers six communes around Bergerac in Dordogne.

france/ruchottes-chambertin.text: A Grand Cru in Gevrey-Chambertin in the Côte de Nuits, making red wine mainly from Pinot Noir. It sits high on the slope above Mazis-Chambertin, and the AOC was created in 1937.

france/rully.text: A Côte Chalonnaise village in Burgundy, about two thirds white from Chardonnay and one third red from Pinot Noir. It has 23 Premier Cru vineyards but no Grand Crus, and the AOC dates from 1939.

france/sacy.text: A Champagne village rated as a cru, in the region that makes Quality Sparkling Wine.

france/saint-amour.text: The northernmost of the ten Beaujolais crus, a red wine made from Gamay. It covers the commune of Saint-Amour-Bellevue, at the southern end of Saône-et-Loire.

france/saint-aubin.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy, about 75% white from Chardonnay and 25% red from Pinot Noir. Its vineyards lie mainly in a side valley west of Chassagne-Montrachet, and it has no Grand Crus.

france/saint-bris.text: A Burgundy appellation in the Grand Auxerrois, near Auxerre in Yonne, for white wine made from Sauvignon, which is unusual in Burgundy. It covers about 250 acres across five communes, southwest of Chablis.

france/saint-chinian.text: A Languedoc-Roussillon appellation for red, rosé and white wines, usually blends of several grapes. Reds can use Syrah, Grenache, Carignan, Mourvèdre and Cinsaut, and whites Marsanne, Roussanne and Vermentino. It has had AOC protection since 1982.

france/saint-emilion.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation for red wine on the Dordogne, around Libourne. Its wines are made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon. It became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.

france/saint-emilion-grand-cru.text: A Bordeaux appellation for red wine, covering nine communes including Saint-Émilion and Libourne. Wines are made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cot and Carmenère.

france/saint-estephe.text: The northernmost of the six communal appellations in the Médoc, in Bordeaux, making red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and other Bordeaux grapes. Five classified growths of 1855 lie within it, and it has been AOC since 1936.

france/saint-georges-saint-emilion.text: A Right Bank Bordeaux appellation for red wine, from the Saint-Georges hamlet in the commune of Montagne. It covered 470 acres in 2005 and is made from Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Cabernet Sauvignon.

france/saint-joseph.text: A northern Rhône appellation, mainly red from Syrah with up to 10% Marsanne or Roussanne. It also makes white from those two grapes. It covers the most land of the northern Rhône, though Crozes-Hermitage has more vines.

france/saint-julien.text: One of the six communal appellations in the Médoc, in Bordeaux, making red wine from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot and other Bordeaux grapes. A number of classified Grand Cru Classé estates lie within it.

france/saint-mont.text: A South West France appellation for wines made from Tannat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Fer and Gros Manseng, with several other grapes allowed. It covers 42 communes in Gers, including Aignan.

france/saint-nicolas-de-bourgueil.text: A Loire Valley appellation on the right bank of the river, making red and rosé from Cabernet Franc, locally called Breton, with up to 10% Cabernet Sauvignon. Rosé is about 2% of output, and the AOC dates from 1937.

france/saint-peray.text: A very small northern Rhône appellation, at its southern end, making white wine only from Marsanne and Roussanne. It makes still wine and a sparkling wine made like Champagne.

france/saint-pourcain.text: A small appellation in Auvergne around Saint-Pourçain-sur-Sioule, upstream of the Loire. It makes white, rosé and red wine from Sacy, Chardonnay, Gamay and Pinot Noir, on about 1,500 acres across 19 communes.

france/saint-romain.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy, making red from Pinot Noir and white from Chardonnay. Its vineyards sit in a side valley west of Auxey-Duresses, toward the Hautes Côtes de Beaune, rather than on the main slope.

france/saint-sardos.text: A South West France appellation for wine made from Tannat and Syrah, with Cabernet Franc and Merlot allowed as minor grapes. It covers 23 communes, including Beaumont-de-Lomagne.

france/saint-veran.text: A Mâconnais appellation in Saône-et-Loire for white Burgundy made only from Chardonnay. It is named after the commune of Saint-Vérand.

france/sainte-croix-du-mont.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers for sweet white wine, made from Sémillon, Sauvignon, Sauvignon Gris and Muscadelle. It comes from a single commune, Sainte-Croix-du-Mont.

france/sainte-foy-bordeaux.text: A Bordeaux appellation in Entre-Deux-Mers allowing red, white and liqueur wine. Reds use Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Cot, and whites Semillon, Sauvignon and Muscadelle. It covers 19 communes, including Caplong and Gensac.

france/sancerre.text: A Loire Valley appellation in the eastern Loire, highly regarded for white wine from Sauvignon Blanc. Red and rosé are also made from Pinot Noir. White Sancerre was one of the original AOCs of 1936.

france/santenay.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy, almost 85% red from Pinot Noir and the rest white from Chardonnay. It covers Santenay and Remigny, and has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/saone-et-loire.text: A French PGI for the Saône-et-Loire département. It grows mostly Chardonnay, about 57% of its vines, followed by Pinot Noir and Gamay.

france/saumur.text: A Loire Valley appellation noted for traditional-method sparkling wine and for reds made mainly from Cabernet Franc. Whites are mainly Chenin Blanc. It covers 33 communes in Maine-et-Loire.

france/saumur-champigny.text: A Loire Valley appellation for red wine made from Cabernet Franc, with Cabernet Sauvignon and Pineau d'Aunis allowed. It covers seven communes, including Montsoreau and Parnay, in Maine-et-Loire.

france/saussignac.text: A Bergerac appellation in South West France making only sweet white wine, similar to Monbazillac but a little drier. It is generally Sémillon affected by noble rot, and adding sugar is forbidden.

france/sauternes.text: A Bordeaux appellation in the Graves section, within Sauternes & Barsac, for sweet white wine from Sémillon, Sauvignon Blanc and Muscadelle, affected by noble rot (Botrytis cinerea). Its climate often brings noble rot, though harvests vary widely between vintages.

france/sauternes-barsac.text: A Bordeaux wine area made up of the Sauternes and Barsac appellations.

france/savennieres.text: A Loire Valley white wine, usually dry, made from Chenin Blanc on three schist hills on the right bank in Anjou-Saumur. It covers about 740 acres in three communes, with two enclave appellations inside it.

france/savennieres-roche-aux-moines.text: A Loire Valley appellation making wine only from Chenin, in the commune of Savennières. Most Loire Valley production is white, from Chenin Blanc, Sauvignon Blanc and Melon.

france/savigny-les-beaune.text: A Côte de Beaune village in Burgundy, slightly over 85% red from Pinot Noir and the rest white from Chardonnay. It is sometimes called simply Savigny, and it has no Grand Cru vineyards.

france/sermiers.text: A Champagne village rated as a cru, in the region that makes Quality Sparkling Wine.

france/sillery.text: A cru village in the Montagne de Reims, a Champagne sub-region with chalk-based soils and nine Grands Crus villages.

france/south-west-france.text: A wine region inland and south of Bordeaux, with about 39,500 acres in separate wine islands along the Dordogne and Garonne rivers and their tributaries. It holds Jurançon, Madiran, Bergerac and Gaillac. In Gers and Lot-et-Garonne, Colombard is the most planted grape.
